steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
In a large mixing bowl cream the butter. Add the flour, sugar and baking soda. Mix until the mixture forms coarse crumbs
Pat 2/3 of the mixture into the bottom of one 9x13 inch baking pan. Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 10 minutes. Remove and let cool slightly.
Spread the lemon curd over the baked layer. To the remaining 1/3 of crumb mixture add the coconut and the almonds. Sprinkle over the top of the lemon curd.
Lower oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bake bars for 25 minutes or until lightly browned.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Curd Bars with Coconut
raw_recipe.description: This bar has the two crusts as requested, and has a strong tangy lemon taste, so much better than most of the lemon bar recipes out there due to the lemon curd and added coconut!
raw_recipe.name: Lemon Curd Bars with Coconut

review.reviewBody: This recipe should have baking powder, not baking soda in the bottom crust. Made many years.

This is delicious and will replace my Lemon Bar recipe! 
For my personal use in the future, this is what I did; I used half butter, half coconut oil in the crust (I made a half batch so it would fit in a 8x8 pan which took 16 minutes to bake), I used about 16 ounces of lemon curd (homemade using my fabulous Pampered Chef recipe)), I followed the directions exactly for the topping. I enjoyed the almonds (which I had chopped up super fine and toasted).
I will continue with my modifications because for me it was perfect.

I made the recipe in a 9x9 pan which yielded a nice thick bar. I omitted the coconut and almonds due to allergies, added the zest of 1 lemon and 6 tbsps extra flour so it wasn't so sticky. I used a scant 2 cups of lemon curd that I had leftover from making tarts. I thought these were a nice way to use up leftover lemon curd and a bit fancier than regular lemon bars. Baked 5 minutes longer for thicker bars. Cut into 16 nice sized bars.

I've never rated a recipe before - but this was so good I had to. I made the following changes: To make the bars thicker, I used a 7 x 11 pan instead of a 9 x 13 pan. And I substituted the zest from 1 lemon for the almonds. I used Dickinson's Lemon Curd. These bars were soooo delicious. I made them for my stepdaughter's birthday (she loves lemon). They were a huge hit -- even with me, and I usually don't like lemon bars.

Ohhhh, so good. Hubs even liked them and he generally doesn't like lemon period...except squeezed on fish. I halved the recipe (used 8x8 pan) and used almost a full can of lemon pie filling, to which I added the juice and zest from half a lemon to freshen it up. Because I knew these would be a more delicate bar dessert, I used sliced almonds rather than chopped, and I was more than pleased with the modifications I made. Rich and buttery, refreshingly lemony, not too sweet, pretty and perfect little dessert.
Tried it without the baking soda, creamed the butter with a hand mixer and it made a super creamy fudge like bottom. Added 1/4 cup of chocolate chips to the topping. They always get raves.

Delicious, although i made many changes! For the crust I used half the butter & added applesauce, reduced the sugar & used baking powder instead of baking soda as some suggested (making it 1/2 c. butter, 1/2 c. applesauce, 2/3 c. sugar & 1/2 tsp. baking powder ). I didn't have almonds, but instead used chopped pecans, and didn't have unsweetened coconut, so used sweetened. It turned out absolutely delicious! 
My jar of lemon curd was 12oz & i agree with others that more would be even better. 
I'll definitely be making these again!

Love! I made these for dessert on Easter and everyone loved them! From the little kids to my parents and their foreign exchange student. I made fresh lemon curd (using the Microwave Lemon Curd recipe).

Super Awesome!! I followed this recipe as is but I increased the fresh lemon juice to 3/4 cup (cause I like the sour zing), I followed another reviewer's advice and made homemade lemon curd (which is equally as yummy and easy to do), besides, I wanted more lemon filling than crust (just my preference), and I did not add the crust on the top, instead I just coated it with coconut and slivered almonds. These bars are super awesome, forget lemon bars, and here on out will be lemon CURD bars!

Hands down our favorite lemon bars! We make our own lemon curd when time permits and use the Honey Roasted Slivered Almonds from Trader Joe’s. As others have recommended, gently press the topping into the curd. These bars are absolutely delicious!! Thank you

We really enjoyed these bars (the only adjustment we made was to omit the baking soda because of other reviewers notes). In the future I would reduce the butter (maybe try 3/4 cup) and put it in a little smaller pan (11x7) because they were very thin bars.
Great recipe I toasted my almonds and coconut before adding to the reserved topping.
I added a pinch of salt and vanilla to the crust. Great recipe. Quick and good
I didn't make any changes. They were good. It was most helpful that I was able to use up the lemon curd that I had made. And I love coconuts so lemon and coconut are just the perfect mix
Everyone who ate them raved at how tasty they were. Have several requests to make more!

Beautiful and special. This recipe is easier than traditional lemon bars, but the addition of coconut and almonds makes it so special. My favorite store bought lemon curd is Trader Joe’s. I will make his again and again.
These were amazing! I made them exactly as shown minus the coconut bc I didn’t have any and used homemade lemon curd. They were a huge hit!
Phenomenal! Made it for potluck at church and they were gone so fast. Everybody loved them!

I made half the recipe in an 8X8 pan. The flavor was very good and as mentioned before the coconut (it's not specified in the recipe but I used unsweetened) and almonds definitely make this shine. Only problem is that my bottom crust didn't set up as well as I would have liked. It may have been just a variation of my oven or the difference from the baking soda vs. baking powder as others have mentioned, but I will pre-bake a few minutes longer next time. And I'm sure the flavor has a lot to do with the quality of lemon curd used. I had some homemade given to me that was delicious and perfectly balanced sweet/tart. I will definitly make it again. As soon as my wonderful sister gives me more lemon curd ;)
Have made it 3 times. I leave out the coconut since kids don't always like it and put in more almond and a little oatmeal. Keeps very well in frig or freezer! Thanks
